entities.summary: Yelena Aleksandrovna Lyubimova was a Soviet geologist known for her geothermal research and as one of the first women geophysicists from the Soviet Union to conduct research in the Atlantic Ocean. She spent her thirty-five year career entirely at the Geophysical Institute. She is known for co-founding the International Committee for Heat Flow, of which she was president from 1971 to 1979. She was also vice-president of the Scientific Council for Geothermal Research.
